# Planned pattern-unit policy validation

**Status: prepared, not executed.** Root runs this after reviewing and freezing
the final source, active inventory/coverage hashes and actual Reference change:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/common-pattern-design/policy-validation/driver.py attempt-01
```

The fixed driver follows the retained source-collection policy procedure,
adding actual inventory and production-coverage regression commands because
this new unit requires a reviewed source/surface metadata refresh. It binds
`pattern.rs` plus the changed frontend module, finite lowerer, sized pattern
view and sized checker. It changes no metadata, production or Reference file.

Planned commands are pinned mdBook 0.5.4 version/build/rendered-link checking;
book, authoring, edition and docs integrity/regressions; constitutional
continuity against `faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2`; current inventory
and coverage guards; and both corresponding mutation suites. Their actual
counts, exits and failures must come from new retained run output. Rust pattern,
ownership, type, effect and public CLI tests are separate root-run work through
the [bounded Rust driver](../validation/driver.py); this policy driver does not
run or assert their success. No Lean build, audit or replay is performed.

Input hashes are collected at execution after root's final barrier. They cover
all production Rust, kernel source, declared docs/governance, selected policy
scripts, active metadata, stdlib and session inventories. This is a declared
incomplete fixture/proof/build-input closure, not binary/Git attestation. New or
changed selected files, the pinned mdBook executable and selected native binary
are checked before/after. Fixture checks themselves validate their referenced
files; this input map does not independently freeze every referenced fixture.

Each retry uses a new attempt directory. Raw stdout/stderr, genuine child
exits, launch failures and timeouts remain unchanged. Only the driver's small
owned temporary mdBook output is removed; its output hashes and real logs remain.
Commands are authored constants, never executed from historical records or
metadata. Concurrent independent Python checks use at most two workers.

Passing guards do not complete a common checker, expose canonical generic QFT,
close an Issue, discharge QS/PR/RS/EXACT or authorize a release. Current route
criteria, pending obligations and both admitted ordinary QLV1 guarantees keep
their existing scopes and statuses.
